name: Net Reproductive Rate Calculator (R₀)
seoTitle: Net Reproductive Rate (R₀) Calculator — Formula & Results
seoDesc: The net reproductive rate is the number of daughters a female leaves over her whole life, and it is the single number that says whether a population will grow
summary:
The net reproductive rate is the number of daughters a female leaves over her whole life, and it is the single number that says whether a population will grow. It returns net reproductive rate, generation time, intrinsic rate of increase and doubling time, and the panel shows all of them at once.

Enter age-specific survival and fertility and it returns R₀, generation time and the per-generation change. The arithmetic keeps full precision internally and only rounds what it displays, so the number you copy out is the number the formula produced. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Net Reproductive Rate (R₀)
sections.html:
R₀ = Σ l(x)·m(x); r ≈ ln R₀ ÷ T; doubling time = ln 2 ÷ r

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
l(x)survival to age xprobability
m(x)daughters produced at age xdaughters
R₀net reproductive ratedaughters per female
Tgeneration timeyears

sections.title: How do I use the Net Reproductive Rate (R₀)?
sections.html:
Fill the boxes you have numbers for; the calculator decides what it can derive from them.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: probability a newborn reaches breeding age of 0.6, daughters per female per season of 3.2 daughters, breeding seasons per lifetime of 2, age at first reproduction of 1 years.

Substituting them into the formula gives net reproductive rate of 3.84 daughters, generation time of 1.5 years, intrinsic rate of increase of 1.35 per year, doubling time of 0.5152 years.

Because the example uses the defaults, you can reproduce it by loading the page and reading the results panel before touching anything.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
Interpretation is a convention, not part of the arithmetic. The usual bands are:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
R₀ < 1Decliningeach female is replaced by less than one daughter
R₀ = 1Stableexact replacement
1 < R₀ < 2Slow growthtypical of long-lived vertebrates
R₀ > 2Fast growthinsects, weeds, invasive species

  • R₀ is a lifetime figure, so it compares across lifespans in a way that r does not; r is the per-year rate and is the one that goes into exponential growth models.

  • The approximation r ≈ ln R₀ / T is exact only in a stable age distribution. When the age structure is disturbed — after a drought or a cull — the realised rate differs for years.

  • A species with R₀ of 1.1 but a generation time of 15 years is effectively static on any management timescale.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
Before blaming the formula, check these — they explain nearly every mismatch:

  • Counting offspring rather than daughters — sons do not add to R₀.
  • Using the mean age at reproduction when reproduction is spread over several seasons.
  • Treating R₀ as a projection: it is an average over the whole life, not next year's growth.

faq.a: The population replaces itself exactly; every female is replaced by one daughter on average.

faq.q: How is R₀ different from the intrinsic rate r?
faq.a: R₀ is per generation and ignores timing; r is per unit time and includes it. A fast-breeding species can have the same R₀ as a slow one but a much larger r.

faq.q: What does the Net Reproductive Rate (R₀) actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns net reproductive rate, generation time, intrinsic rate of increase and doubling time. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
